title: Brave Search MCP Server
summary: Give your coding agent live web, news, image and local search through Brave's own MCP server, so it can look up current docs and errors.
description: Brave publishes this server for its Search API. It exposes tools such as brave_web_search, brave_news_search, brave_local_search, brave_image_search and brave_video_search, plus a summarizer and an LLM context tool.
It runs on your machine through npx over stdio. The only thing it needs is a Brave Search API key, which you create in the Brave API dashboard and keep in an environment variable.
Reach for it when the model's training data is too old: a library released last month, an error message you have never seen, or a question about a recent change.
useWhen: Look up the newest release notes for a dependency
Search for the exact text of an obscure error message
Check recent news about a vendor outage
Find a nearby business or place while planning a trip

mcp.name: brave-search

env.name: BRAVE_API_KEY
env.description: Your Brave Search API key from the Brave API dashboard

access: Sends your search queries to the Brave Search API
Reads search results only; it changes nothing on your machine

example.prompt: Search the web for the changelog of the latest Vite major version and list the breaking changes.
example.result: Found the official Vite release notes. Breaking changes: the minimum Node version was raised, a default browser target changed, and one deprecated plugin hook was removed. Source links are listed below each item.

faq.question: Does it cost money?
faq.answer: The server is free, but each search counts against your Brave Search API plan. Check the plan limits in the Brave dashboard before letting an agent loop on searches.

faq.question: Can I turn some tools off?
faq.answer: Yes. The server reads BRAVE_MCP_ENABLED_TOOLS and BRAVE_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLS, so you can keep only web search if you do not want image or video results.

faq.question: Why stdio and not the HTTP mode?
faq.answer: The HTTP mode opens a local port with no authentication, so stdio is the safer default for a single developer machine.

access: Sends search queries to Brave over the network
Needs an API key in BRAVE_API_KEY
